items.title: Al Gallodoro Interview, 1966-05-10
items.q: Ralph Herman did the concerto for doubles for band... Ralph Herman had been writing for Manna albums, you know, arranging for the singers and so forth. He says, Al, they would like to try something different. They would like to record the concerto for doubles.

ctx.x: Isn't that about a horse? Yes.

What did you read about it? When I was little. Yes, that's right. But it's supposed to be a very good picture and I imagine it's a clean one for a change. Yeah. The scenery is great. The score is very good. It's modern but... Who wrote the score? Oh, born... Not Herman, you didn't know? No, no. I'll have to think of the fellow's name. Young fellow. About 30, 35. But the music is good. I have a few solos here and there. Did you do any with Andre Previn and his score?
Oh, he's got to answer that.

items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: Ralph Herman was arranging for the company... Ralph said, 'Why don’t we do something different? Al Gallodoro just performed a ‘Concerto for Doubles’... Why don’t we do this?'

ctx.x: And they were heavy to carry around.

That’s right and they were scratchy. But some 78s were not as scratchy as others. My original recording of “Concerto for Doubles,” I’m glad I’m thinking of this, we had a 50 piece orchestra. Manor. M-A-N-O-R. They were on 57th Street just west of Broadway or Eighth Avenue. Sam Lyra and his partner. Ralph Herman was arranging for the company for different singers, and Ralph said, “Why don’t we do something different? Al Gallodoro just performed a ‘Concerto for Doubles’ that Paul Whiteman had written for him. Why…
Yeah. I think I do. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
